name: MLOps & Model Deployment
description: Packaging, deploying, tracking and monitoring machine learning models in production with reproducible, automated workflows.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of an experiment tracking tool such as MLflow Tracking?
options: To label training data
To write model code automatically
To record parameters, metrics and artifacts of training runs so they can be compared and reproduced
To replace version control for source code
questions.explanation: Experiment tracking logs each run's configuration and results, enabling comparison and reproducibility.

questions.question: Why is a trained model often packaged into a Docker container for deployment?
options: It bundles the model with its exact dependencies so it runs consistently across environments
It makes the model more accurate
It removes the need for a server
It automatically retrains the model
questions.explanation: Containers capture the runtime environment, avoiding 'works on my machine' problems.

questions.question: What is data drift?
options: Data being moved between cloud regions
Gradual corruption of files on disk
The model's weights changing after deployment
A change in the distribution of input data in production compared with the training data
questions.explanation: When production inputs shift away from the training distribution, model performance can degrade even though the model itself is unchanged.

questions.question: What is the role of a model registry?
options: Storing raw training data
Managing versioned models and their lifecycle stages, such as staging and production
Hosting the team's source code
Generating synthetic features
questions.explanation: A model registry provides a central store for model versions, lineage, and promotion between stages.

questions.question: What is training-serving skew?
options: A difference between how features are computed at training time and at inference time, causing degraded predictions
When the training job uses more GPUs than the serving job
When serving latency exceeds training time
When the model is trained on more data than it serves
questions.explanation: Inconsistent feature pipelines between training and serving (e.g. different preprocessing code) silently hurt production accuracy; feature stores and shared pipelines help prevent it.

questions.question: In a canary deployment of a new model version, what happens?
options: The old model is deleted immediately and replaced
The new model is only run offline on historical data
Both models are retrained together
A small fraction of live traffic is routed to the new model while its metrics are monitored before a full rollout
questions.explanation: Canary releases limit risk by exposing the new version to a small share of traffic first and rolling back if metrics degrade.

practical.title: Log a training run with MLflow
practical.instructions: Write a short Python snippet that, inside an MLflow run, logs the hyperparameter max_depth=5, logs the metric accuracy (stored in a variable acc), and logs a trained scikit-learn model stored in a variable model.
practical.expected_output: import mlflow; with mlflow.start_run(): mlflow.log_param('max_depth', 5); mlflow.log_metric('accuracy', acc); mlflow.sklearn.log_model(model, 'model')

tasks.title: Understand the MLOps lifecycle
tasks.description: Study the MLOps roadmap and the MLflow overview docs. Summarize the stages of experiment tracking, packaging, deployment and monitoring.
tasks.completion_criteria: One-page summary describing each lifecycle stage and a tool used for it.

tasks.title: Track experiments with MLflow
tasks.description: Instrument an existing scikit-learn training script with MLflow tracking. Run it with several hyperparameter values and compare runs in the MLflow UI.
tasks.completion_criteria: At least 5 logged runs with parameters, metrics and a saved model artifact.

tasks.title: Serve a model as a containerized API
tasks.description: Wrap a trained model in a FastAPI prediction endpoint with input validation. Write a Dockerfile, build the image and call the endpoint from the command line.
tasks.completion_criteria: Docker container runs locally and returns predictions for a sample request.

tasks.title: Build an automated ML pipeline with monitoring
tasks.description: Create a Git repository with a CI workflow that tests, trains and registers a model, then deploys the container. Add basic monitoring that logs prediction inputs and flags data drift.
tasks.completion_criteria: CI pipeline runs on push, model is versioned in a registry, and a drift report is generated from logged inputs.
